# netbox_region (Resource)

From the [official documentation](https://docs.netbox.dev/en/stable/features/sites-and-racks/#regions):

> Sites can be arranged geographically using regions. A region might represent a continent, country, city, campus, or other area depending on your use case. Regions can be nested recursively to construct a hierarchy. For example, you might define several country regions, and within each of those several state or city regions to which sites are assigned.
>
> Each region must have a name that is unique within its parent region, if any.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netbox_region" "test" {
  name        = "test"
  description = "test description"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the region.

### Optional

- `comments` (String) Free-form comments about the region.
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values of the object, as a map of field name to value.
- `description` (String) A description of the region.
- `owner_id` (Number) The ID of the owner associated with the region. Needs NetBox 4.5.0 or later.
- `parent_region_id` (Number) The ID of the parent region associated with the region.
- `slug` (String) The URL-friendly slug of the region.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags assigned to the object, by name.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String) When the region was created.
- `id` (String) The numeric ID of the region.
- `last_updated` (String) When the region was last changed.
- `prefix_count` (Number) The number of prefix objects that refer to the region.
- `site_count` (Number) The number of site objects that refer to the region.
- `tags_all` (Set of String) All tags assigned to the object, including those not managed by Terraform.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the numeric NetBox ID of the object
terraform import netbox_region.example 1
```
